There is no distinction between finding them in the marketplace and finding them among one's own papers where the finder is not a third party and does not remember having received them in trust.
Even if there are no witnesses on it. This is specifically where the debt document itself is also in the third party's possession, as the ruling continues to explain.
And specifically where the document is in his possession together with the receipt, etc. The Sema, seif katan 65, writes that where the debt document is in the third party's possession together with the receipt, even if the third party does not know whether it was paid, we presume it paid, as in the case where the third party died. The opening words, "and he says that it was paid," concern a signed receipt, where there is no need for the debt document itself to be in his possession. So too write the Bach and the Ir Shushan. They must mean that the debt document is then torn up, for otherwise it is obvious that neither document would be returned to either party, as explained at the beginning of this siman. They wrote this in order to resolve the Beit Yosef's question: if the third party himself says it was paid, why does it matter that he also holds the receipt? But their explanation is not compelled. The same difficulty the Beit Yosef raised against the Baal HaTerumos can be raised against Tosafos at the end of Perek Zeh Borer, in their first explanation that a simpon found in a third party's possession is valid where the debt document is together with the simpon. I cited their words above at the beginning of siman 56. Hagahos Ashri there already answers that the simpon serves merely as a memorandum, and Maharshal says the same. The Baal HaTerumos and Tur can therefore be explained in this way as well. This interpretation fits the wording of Baal HaTerumos better, contrary to the Bach's criticism of the Beit Yosef in seif 27. The Bach writes that Baal HaTerumos also speaks where the third party says nothing, but that is incorrect, for Baal HaTerumos explicitly says, "when he says it is paid, he is believed." Nevertheless, Hagahos Mordechai at the end of the first chapter of Bava Metzia cites Rabbeinu Tam's explanation concerning an unsigned simpon where the debt document also emerges from the third party's possession. Even if the third party does not know whether it was paid, but merely remembers that a receipt was delivered to him, we say that because the creditor delivered the debt document to him as well, the debt was certainly paid. It appears that Rabbeinu Tam intended thereby to answer why the simpon was needed, as the Sema and Bach explain the Tur. According to this, the creditor must deny having delivered the receipt to the third party, for otherwise why does the Gemara at the end of Perek Zeh Borer ask, "this proves that a third party is believed, etc."? Still, it is possible that Hagahos Mordechai speaks specifically where the third party is alive. If he died, perhaps the receipt would have no effect, because who says that the creditor delivered this particular receipt to him? Yet the Rambam in chapter 16 of Hilchos Malveh, cited by the Mechaber above in siman 56, end of seif 1, states explicitly that even if the third party died and a written notation is found with him stating that the debt document deposited with him was paid, the debt is treated as paid even though no witnesses signed the notation. It appears that the Rambam follows Rabbeinu Tam's explanation, which is Tosafos' first explanation at the end of Perek Zeh Borer, as I wrote above in siman 56, seif katan 12, and uses it to answer why a simpon is needed. He therefore establishes the baraita where the third party died and holds that since the third party did not tear up the simpon, it is as though he were alive and saying that the simpon is valid. Since the parties appointed him as a third party, he should not have left the receipt intact if it were invalid. The Gemara's question, "this proves that a third party is believed," is therefore appropriate. Tosafos may also have intended this. One should not explain that Tosafos speaks of a simpon written in the third party's own handwriting in the form of testimony by the third party, because that is not the plain meaning of the baraita. See there carefully. Nor is there a difficulty from the Rambam, Baal HaTerumos, Tur, and Mechaber above in seif 8, who rule that where one finds a document, even with a simpon, the debt document must specifically be among torn documents. That case concerns one who found it in the marketplace or among his own papers and is not a third party at all. We may therefore say that the document and receipt both fell from the creditor, who had prepared the receipt for the time when the debtor would pay. Here, by contrast, both are found in the possession of a person who is known to have been appointed as third party, or the creditor admits his appointment. The receipt therefore necessarily came to him from the creditor as well. If the debt were not paid, why did the creditor deliver the receipt to him? He should have deposited only the debt document. See what I wrote above in siman 56, seif katan 12 and seif katan 13.
And if it is not authenticated, it shall be authenticated through its signatures. The Tur means that once it is authenticated, the third party is believed to say that it is paid. The Mechaber omitted this because he follows his own question in the Beit Yosef: if the receipt is authenticated, what need is there for the third party's credibility? His objection is incorrect, as Darkei Moshe, Sema, Bach, and the other later authorities have already noted. The meaning is that at present the receipt is not authenticated. Therefore we need the third party to say that it is paid, and then, if the signatures can be authenticated, or once they are in fact authenticated, he is believed afterward to say that it was paid. This remains true even though beit din already saw the receipt in his possession and he therefore lacks a migo, because he previously could have given it to the debtor. The case concerns one who is known to have been appointed as third party, or where the creditor admits it, and thereby trusted him, as I wrote above in seif katan 63. The receipt is then given to the debtor and the debt document is torn. But if the third party says nothing, the receipt would not be given to the debtor while it remains unauthenticated; it would simply be left deposited. Therefore, if the third party dies, neither document is returned to either side. The case is where the receipt is unauthenticated but capable of authentication. If it were authenticated while in the third party's possession, it would obviously be returned to the debtor, because it would be returned even if found in the creditor's own possession, as above at the end of seif 18. If it could not be authenticated at all, it would obviously be ineffective. This resolves the words of the Raavad cited by Baal HaTerumos, Shaar 53, part 3: if the debt document itself was not given to him in trust, the receipt is ineffective, because who says the creditor made him a third party? Perhaps he is lying. But if the receipt itself was deposited with him as third party, the third party is believed where witnesses are signed on it and their signatures are authenticated, because the receipt certainly passed from the creditor's possession into the third party's possession. Therefore, even without witnesses to payment, the third party is believed. The Beit Yosef cites this. Gidulei Terumah asks: if the signatures are authenticated, we already know the debt is paid without relying on the third party. According to what I have written, there is no difficulty. The case is where the signatures are authenticated now, not where a formal authentication was written on the receipt itself. Proof is that otherwise, how could the Raavad say that it certainly passed from the creditor's possession? On the contrary, if it were formally authenticated, it would certainly have passed from the debtor's possession, as stated in the Gemara. Further, why was it necessary to say that it certainly passed from the creditor? Rather, his meaning is that because witnesses are signed upon it, one cannot say, "who says the creditor made him a third party?" The receipt necessarily passed from the creditor to the third party. This is clear. Still, it appears that when the Raavad says that it certainly passed from the creditor, he means that the creditor himself is forced to admit that it came from him once witnesses are signed and their signatures can be authenticated. Even if the creditor does not admit this, the third party is believed that it came from the creditor through a migo that he could have handed it to the debtor, provided that beit din did not previously see the receipt in his possession. If, however, the creditor denies having appointed him as third party at all and says that the receipt, or the document together with the receipt, fell from him and this person found it, and beit din already saw the receipt in the third party's possession so that he has no migo, the third party is not believed to invalidate the debt document. His law is then that of one who finds a document, and neither document is returned to either party. This appears correct to me.
It shall be authenticated through its signatures. But if it cannot be authenticated, it is ineffective, as I wrote immediately above. This is also evident from the Tur, and the Sema, seif katan 66, writes the same, contrary to Maadanei Melech at the end of the first chapter of Bava Metzia. Maadanei Melech understands the Tur to mean that even if it is not authenticated, the third party is believed because authentication of documents is rabbinic, while Torah law does not require authentication, and in the case of a third party the Sages left the law at its Torah level. He writes that this follows from the plain meaning of the baraita and the Rosh, and challenges the Sema. His words are incorrect. Nothing of the sort is proved from the baraita or Rosh, for they can be speaking where the document will later be authenticated. He also overlooked the words of the Tur and Mechaber above in siman 56, seif 4, that an instrument is ineffective where authentication is impossible. What Maadanei Melech further writes, that Nimukei Yosef explicitly says at the end of the first chapter of Bava Metzia that the case concerns a receipt without witnesses to authentication, likewise proves nothing. Even if there is no formal authentication on the receipt itself, the case can specifically be one where its signatures are capable of authentication. Still, in my humble opinion the practical law requires study for another reason. Nimukei Yosef at the end of Perek Zeh Borer explicitly states that even if the witnesses to the receipt are presently unavailable for authentication, the receipt is effective even where the third party has no migo, because once the parties trusted him as third party and the signatures could have been authenticated at one time, he is believed. See there. I also proved above in siman 56, seif katan 1, that Tosafos at the end of Perek Zeh Borer holds the same, contrary to the Bach's understanding of Tosafos here. The Bach's objection to Tosafos from the sugya at the end of the first chapter of Bava Metzia is likewise no difficulty. Tosafos does not accept Rashi's explanation there. Rather, the baraita's phrase, "it shall be authenticated through its signatures," does not mean that a formal authentication is already written on it, because the language, "it shall be authenticated," would not fit. It means that the witnesses themselves are questioned. See there carefully.
Even though the debtor admits. The Sema, seif katan 69, writes that if the creditor admits that the debt was paid, the receipt is returned to the debtor, as he wrote earlier in seif 18, seif katan 58. I already challenged him there in seif katan 49. Accordingly, here, since the debt document has been impaired as explained below, even if the creditor admits payment the receipt is not returned to the debtor, because perhaps the debtor will return it to the creditor.
Because we are concerned for collusion, etc. The Bach, in seif 28, asks against the Tur. Above in seif 5 the Tur cites the Rosh that with a deposited document that has suffered no defect we do not suspect collusion. The same difficulty arises against the Mechaber, who cites the Rosh's view in seif 3. The Bach answers that there the depositary is alive but does not remember from whom the document came, whereas here he died and the document left his possession. Gidulei Terumah, Shaar 52, end of part 3, writes similarly. This distinction is incorrect. The plain wording of the Tur and Mechaber above implies that the same law applies even if the third party died. Rather, there was never any difficulty. Here, the receipt was at least deposited with a third party. If it came from the debtor, the debt document is void. If it came from the creditor, the debt document has been impaired because the creditor deposited the receipt with the third party. What could one answer, that with a deposited item no defect arose? If we say that no defect arose, then all the more the receipt remains valid and the debt document is void. That is why above in seif 18, when the debtor admits the debt is unpaid, the receipt is returned to the creditor. There, no defect arose in the debt document, because perhaps the receipt fell from the creditor after he had merely prepared it in anticipation of payment. Here, by contrast, the creditor at least deposited the receipt with the third party, and it is known that he appointed him as such, or the creditor admits this. The debt document is therefore impaired, because the creditor may have deposited the receipt with him for delivery to the debtor. The Bach himself writes something similar above in seif 23, though briefly and without fully explaining it. It is surprising that his words contradict each other. It appears further that if the creditor does not admit appointing him as third party, but says that he lost the receipt and the deceased person found it, the debt document is not impaired at all. Its law is the same as a receipt found in the marketplace. If the debtor admits the debt remains unpaid, the receipt is returned to the creditor. This appears clear to me.
Therefore collection is not made with the debt document. This means collection from encumbered property, even though the debtor admits the debt.

urim_vetumim_tumim.he: ודוקא ששטר בידו עם השובר עיי' אורים שהעליתי כסמ"ע וב"ח דאפי' א"י אם פרוע או לא מכל מקום הואיל ושטר ושובר בידו אתרע וא"ל לפי' רש"י דפי' נמצא שטר וא"י מה טיבו קאי על שליש אם כן מה דוחקא דגמ' לפרש הך סיפא ואם יש עמהם סמפון ענין בפ"ע ומוסב על מלוה והקשו הא שובר פסול ביוצא מתחת יד המלוה ואיצטרך לשנוי' בנמצא בשטרות קרועי' ולא משני דמוסב על שליש דאם יש עמו סמפון יעשה מה שבסמפון וא"צ לדוחק כלל דבשליש א"צ לשטר שיהיה בשטרות קרועי' דבר זה בבעה"ת שער נ"ב ח"ג דין יו"ד ובסופו מיושב דדייק ליה הגמרא מדקתני אם יש עמהם ולא קתני אם יש עמו דהוי משמע אדלעיל קאי בלשון יחיד מצא שטר וכו' אלא דהוא ענין נפרד ומוסב על שטרותיו של בעה"ב ולא קאי אדלעיל אשליש ושפיר פריך הגמרא
urim_vetumim_tumim.en: And specifically where the document is in his possession together with the receipt. See Urim, where I concluded like the Sema and Bach that even if the third party does not know whether the debt was paid, once both the promissory note and the receipt are in his possession the document is weakened. One should not ask, according to Rashi, who explains "a document was found and its status is unknown" as referring to a third party, why the Gemara did not explain the later clause, "if there is a receipt with them, follow the receipt," as continuing the same third party case. It would then be unnecessary to establish the receipt as found among torn documents. Baal HaTerumot, gate 52, part 3, law 10, resolves this from the wording. The Mishnah says "if there is with them," in the plural, rather than "if there is with it," in the singular, which would naturally refer back to the single document held by the third party. The Gemara therefore understood the clause as a separate case concerning the owner's group of documents, and properly asked how a receipt in the creditor's possession can have force.

urim_vetumim_urim.he:
אפילו ראו כבר בידו וכו' דשליש מהימן אפי' לית ליה מגו הואיל והימני' תחילה כדלעיל סי' נ"ו באריכות ואפילו מכחיש שלא עשאו שליש כמ"ש בסי' נ"ו ע"ש:
ודוקא ששטר בידו וכו' ואפי' אומר השליש בעצמו שא"י אם פרע אם לאו מ"מ אתרע הואיל ושטר שוב' בצדו ועיין ש"ך דיש חולקים בזה ולדינא נר' עיקר כסמ"ע וב"ח ועיין תומים מ"ש בישובו:
ואם אינו מקוים וכו' פי' אם אפשר לקיימו אם כן אף דאינו מקוים דאם הוא כבר מקוים אין צריך לנאמנותו של שליש דודאי של לוה הוא רק אינו מקוים אך הואיל ואפשר לקיימו השליש נאמן במאמרו דמתחילה הימני' דהא אפשר לקיימו אבל אם א"א לקיימו אם כן לא הימני' דהא אף אלו מסרו ביד לוה לא היה מועיל כמ"ש לעיל בסי' מ"ו וש"ך האריך בכאן להיות נמשך אחרי דברי הנ"י דס"ל אם מודה שאינו מזויף אף דא"א לקיימו מכל מקום השליש נאמן וכבר בררתי לעיל כי הנ"י נמשך אחרי דברי רש"י אבל לדעת התוס' ורוב הפוסקים ליתא לדברי הנ"י וכ"כ דא"א לקיימו לא שייך הימני' בשליש כלל ועיין מש"ל סי' נ"ו:
לפי שחוששים לקנוניא ואעפ"י דס"ל לרא"ש היכא דלא נפל ולא אתרע לא חוששי' לקנוניא התם בשטר ביד שליש מהכ"ת נימא דפרע כיון דחייב מודה דלא פרע ומאין הרגלים לומר דיש קנוניא אבל כאן דשובר לפניך ועדים אמרו דפרע אם כן הלוה דאומר דלא נפרע ומכחיש משמעות של השובר הרי כאן ריעותא כמו בנפל ולכ"ע חיישינן לקנוניא ועיין ש"ך ואולי כיון למ"ש וש"ך ביקש לחלק אם מודה בשלישית או לא ולא נר' כן לדינא דהעלינו לעיל כדברי סמ"ע דאפי' בנמצא בשוק ולוה מודה חוששי' לקנוניא ומכ"ש ביד שליש:
urim_vetumim_urim.en:
Even if they had already seen it in his possession, etc. A third party is believed even without a migo because the parties initially trusted him, as explained at length above in siman 56. This is so even if one party denies ever appointing him as third party, as I wrote there. See there.
Specifically when the document is in his possession, etc. Even if the third party himself says that he does not know whether payment occurred, the debt is nevertheless weakened because the receipt is beside the document. See Shach, who cites dissenters. As practical law, the primary view appears to be that of Sema and Bach. See Tumim for my resolution.
If it is not validated, etc. Meaning where it is capable of validation. If it were already validated, the third party's credibility would be unnecessary, because it would certainly belong to the borrower. Rather, it is presently unvalidated, but because it can be validated, the third party is believed by virtue of the trust initially placed in him. If, however, it cannot possibly be validated, then the parties did not rely on him regarding it, because even had he delivered it directly to the borrower it would have had no effect, as I wrote above in siman 46. Shach discusses at length here, following Nimukei Yosef, who holds that if the lender admits the receipt is not forged, then even though formal validation is impossible the third party is believed. I already established above that Nimukei Yosef follows Rashi's approach. According to Tosafos and most poskim, Nimukei Yosef's position is not accepted. Where validation is impossible, the special trust in a third party does not apply at all. See what I wrote above in siman 56.
Because we suspect collusion. Although Rosh holds that where a document was not lost and therefore not weakened we do not suspect collusion, that is because with an ordinary document held by a third party there is no basis to say payment occurred when the debtor admits it did not. Here, however, a receipt lies before us and witnesses say that payment occurred. The borrower's claim that there was no payment contradicts the implication of the receipt, creating an irregularity comparable to a lost document. Everyone therefore suspects collusion. See Shach. Perhaps this is his intention. Shach sought to distinguish based on whether the borrower admits the third party arrangement, but this does not appear correct as law. We concluded above with Sema that even where a document is found in the marketplace and the borrower admits the debt, collusion is suspected. Certainly it is suspected where the document is held by a third party.

mechaber.he: (ל' רמב"ם פט"ז מה' מלוה דין י' כל הסעיף) שטר שנמצא בו שובר בגוף השטר בין מלפניו בין מלאחריו ואפי' במקצתו שטר זה פרוע או שנפרע ממנו כך וכך אפי' יוצא מתחת ידי המלוה ואע"פ שאין על הכתב עדים עושים כמו שכתוב בשובר (וה"ה אם מצא כתוב בפנקסו שטר פלוני הוא פרוע) (ר"י נ"י ח"ד):

baer_hetev.he:
במקצתו. פי' הסמ"ע דמקצת השובר נכתב נגד השטר ומקצתו למטה ממנו לאפוקי אם היה כולו למט' ממנו דאינו כלום דאי בעי גייז ליה והשטר נשאר בשלימותו מיהו דוקא כשהמלו' חי וטוען ברי שאינו פרוע אבל כשנפטר אף אם השובר כולו למטה ממנו אין גובין בשטר זה והש"ך השיג על פירושו וכתב דהעיקר שצ"ל ואפי' בקצתו ופירש אפילו בקצ' השטר כו' ע"ש (וכעין זה פירש הט"ז והשיג גם כן על הסמ"ע ע"ש):
עדים. וגם אין עליו חת"י המלו' וכנ"ל. סמ"ע:
מצא. ורבי ירוחם כתב ונמצא כתוב בפנקסו כו' ור"ל שאחרים מצאו כן וא"ש טפי דתו ליכא מגו וכ"נ להגיה בדברי הרמ"א. שם:
baer_hetev.en:
somewhat. It was written against the barrage, and it was a bit down from it to the duke, if it were all to the point where he was not wild, but when the entire break was removed from him, he had no understanding of it, and that he had not been given to him
Witnesses. Also, the document does not bear the lender's signature, as explained above. Sema.
Found. Rabbeinu Yerucham writes, 'and it was found written in his ledger,' meaning that others found it there. This wording is preferable, because there is then no migo. It likewise appears that the Rama's text should be emended accordingly. Sema.

beer_hagolah.he: ו) ברייתא שם דף כ"א ע"א וכדמפרש שם בגמרא דאי לאו דפרעיה לא הוה מרעי שטרי:
beer_hagolah.en: A baraita there, 21a, as the Gemara explains: had he not repaid it, he would not have impaired his document.

beur_hagra.he:
בין כו'. שם ק"ג א':
ואפי' בקצתו. כצ"ל ועש"ך והוא שם סוף פ"א אחר חיתום כו':
(ליקוט) במקצתו. צ"ל בקצתו ר"ל אפי' במקום שיכול לגייז וכמ"ש אחר חיתום כו' ועב"ב קס"ד א' אי מלתחת כו' ועהג"א ספ"ג דסנה' ד"ה פי' כשהוא כתוב כו' (ע"כ):
או שנפרע. שם קג א':
ואע"פ שם סוף פ"א וכפי' הראשון של תוס' דסנה' הנ"ל:
beur_hagra.en:
Whether... There, 103a.
Even in part of it. This is the correct reading. See the Shach. It is at the end of the first chapter there, "after the signatures..."
(Collected note) In part of it. It should read "in part of it," meaning even in a place where it could be cut off, as stated regarding a notation after the signatures. See Bava Batra 164a, and Hagahos Ashri at the end of the third chapter of Sanhedrin, s.v. peirush k'shehu kasuv. (End of note.)
Or that it was paid. There, 103a.
Even though. There at the end of the first chapter, according to Tosafos' first explanation in Sanhedrin cited above.

meirat_einayim.he:
ואפילו במקצתו. כן הוא לשון הרמב"ם ונרא' דר"ל דמקצת השובר נכתב נגד השטר ומקצתו למטה ממנו לאפוקי אם היה כולו למטה ממנו דאינו כלום דאי בעי גייז ליה והשטר נשאר בשלימותו והיינו דוקא כשהמלוה עצמו חי וטוען ברי שאינו פרוע משא"כ כשנפטר דאף אם השובר כולו למטה ממנו במקום דיכול לחתכן אין גובין בשטר זה ובזה מיושב מ"ש בסעיף שאחר זה ראובן נפטר כו' עושין כמ"ש בשובר דקשה מאי קמ"ל הא אף אם המלוה חי וטוען ברי שאינו פרוע הדין כן אלא ודאי קמ"לן שם דאף שנכתב השובר במקום שיכול לחתכו עושין כמו שכתוב בשובר כיון שהן יתומים וטוענין שמא דאין טענינן בזה עבורם משא"כ כשהוא חי וטוען ברי דכתב כאן דצריך שיהא נכתב השובר במקום שאי אפשר לחתכו ודו"ק ולפי זה צריך לומר דמ"ש בין מלפניו מיירי שכתב שם באופן שאינו יכול לחותכו דהיינו ביני שיטי וק"ל ובמצאו כתוב בפנקסו דמחזקינן בפרוע דכל מה שכתוב בפנקסו הוה כאלו העיד עליו שהוא כן וכמ"ש בדרישה שוב ראיתי בר' ירוחם דכתב שם ונמצא כתוב בפנקסו ור"ל שאחרים מצאו כן כתוב וא"ש טפי דתו ליכא מגו וק"ל וכן נראה להגיה בדברי מור"ם "ונמצא במקום "ומצא ועמ"ש בסעיף שאחר זה:
ואע"פ שאין על הכתב עדים פי' וגם אין עליו חתימת יד המלוה וכנ"ל:
עושים כמ"ש בשובר שאם לא היה פרוע לא היה כותב אותו בגוף השטר:
meirat_einayim.en:
And even partially. This is the Rambam's language. It appears that he means that part of the receipt is written opposite the debt instrument and part below it. This excludes a case where the entire receipt is written below the instrument, in which case it is ineffective because the creditor could simply cut it off and leave the debt instrument intact. This applies specifically when the creditor himself is alive and makes a definite claim that the debt was not paid. If he has died, however, then even if the entire receipt is written below the instrument in a place where it could be cut off, collection may not be made with this debt instrument. This resolves the difficulty in the next seif, which states, "Reuven died, etc.; we act in accordance with what is written in the receipt." What novelty does that teach, since even if the creditor were alive and made a definite claim that the debt was not paid, the law would seemingly be the same? Rather, the novelty there is that even when the receipt is written in a place where it could be cut off, we act according to it because the claimants are orphans who can only claim uncertainty. We do not advance for them the argument that the receipt should be disregarded. When the creditor is alive and makes a definite claim, however, the rule stated here requires that the receipt be written in a place from which it cannot be cut off. According to this, the phrase "whether on its front" must concern a case where it was written in a manner that cannot be cut away, such as between the lines. Regarding a notation found in his ledger, we presume the debt to have been paid because everything written in his ledger is as though he himself testified that it is so, as I wrote in the Derishah. I later saw that Rabbeinu Yerucham writes, "and it was found written in his ledger," meaning that others found it so written. This is even more satisfactory, because there is then no migo. It therefore appears that the Rama's text should be emended to read "and it was found" instead of "and he found." See what I write in the next seif.
Even though there are no witnesses on the writing. Meaning, it also does not bear the creditor's signature, as explained above.
Do as a “cash” in the voucher that if it weren’t wild, he wouldn’t have written it in the hay body:

netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.he:
במקצתו. פי' שמקצת השובר נכתב נגד השטר ומקצתו למטה לאפוקי אם היה כולו למטה אינו כלום ונאמן במיגו דאי בעי היה גייז ליה. מיהו דוקא כשהמלוה חי וטוען ברי שלא נפרע אבל אם מת לא מעני' ליורשיו. והש"ך והט"ז הסכימו דאפילו כולו למטה כשר השובר ואפי' חי דהוי מיגו במקום חזקה דאילו לא נפרע לא היה מרע לשטרא:
עדים. וגם אין עליו ח"י המלוה סמ"ע:
מצא. בסמ"ע הגיה ונמצא שאחרים מצאו דליכא מיגו:
netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.en:
In part of it. Meaning, part of the receipt is written opposite the text of the debt document and part below it. This excludes a receipt written entirely below the document, which according to this view has no effect because the creditor is believed through a migo that he could have cut it off. This applies specifically when the creditor is alive and makes a definite claim that he was not paid. If he died, we do not advance such a claim for the heirs. The Shach and Taz agree that even a receipt written entirely below is valid, including while the creditor is alive, because the migo is opposed by a strong presumption. Had he not been paid, he would not ordinarily have weakened his own document by allowing a receipt to be written there:
Witnesses. There is also no signature of the lender on it, Sema:
He found it. The Sema emends the text to mean that others found it, so there is no migo available to the creditor:

siftei_kohen.he:
ואפי' במקצתו כו'. הוא ל' הרמב"ם. ומה שפי' הסמ"ע דר"ל שמקצת השובר נכתב נגד השטר ומקצתו למטה ממנו לאפוקי אם היה כולו למטה ממנו אינו כלום דאי בעי גייז ליה כו' לא נהירא והעיקר שצ"ל ואפי' בקצתו וכן העתיק להדיא בבעה"ת שער נ"ג ל' הרמב"ם ופירושו אפי' בקצה השטר דאל"כ היאך לא יכתוב הרמב"ם דין סמפון היוצא לאחר חיתום שטרות שבש"ס ויכתוב דין אחר מה שלא נזכר בש"ס כלל וכן פסק להדיא בהגהת אשרי פ' זה בורר דלא אמרינן מגו דאי בעי גייז ליה וכ"פ הב"ח ע"ש שהאריך וכן הוא בתשובת הרמב"ן סימן ק' וז"ל וכדתניא סמפון היוצא לאחר חיתום שטרות כשר דאי לאו דפריע לא הוה מרע לשטרי' וההוא ודאי אי בעי גייז ליה כו' וע"ש ועיין מ"ש בסעיף שאח"ז ס"ק ע"ג:
וה"ה אם מצא כתוב בפינקסו כו'. ע"ל סי' צ"א סעיף ה' מ"ש שם:
siftei_kohen.en:
Even at its edge, etc. This is the Rambam’s language. The Sema’s explanation, that part of the receipt must be written opposite the text of the document and part below it, is incorrect. The correct reading is ‘even at its edge,’ as Baal HaTerumot expressly quotes the Rambam. Otherwise the Rambam would have omitted the Gemara’s rule of a receipt written after the witnesses’ signatures and substituted a case not mentioned there. Hagahot Ashri, the Bach, and the Ramban all rule that we do not accept the migo that the creditor could have cut off the receipt. If the debt had not been paid, he would not have impaired his own document in this manner.
"And if you find it in your mouth." . . . . .

urim_vetumim_tumim.he: ואפי' במקצתו דעת הסמ"ע דוקא דשובר נכתב במקום דא"א לחתכו אבל במקום דאפשר לחתכו נאמן דלא נפרע במגו דהיה גייז לי' וש"ך הביא בשם הגהת הרא"ש דלא שייך מגו דהוי מגו במקום חזקה ואמת שכתב כן הגהת הרא"ש אבל הביאו בשם הר"ב מרעגנשבורג דחולק ונר' דכן הוא דעת תוס' בסנהדרין דף ל"א ע"ב ד"ה אין עליו עדים בהא דפרכי' ללישנא בתרא דבעי' בשליש מגו מהא דתנן אין עליו עדים ויוצא מתחת יד שליש וכ' תוס' דליכא למימר דמיירי בלי אתחזק בב"ד דדומי' דיוצא לאחר חתום שטרות קתני וי"ל דילמא הך נמי איירי בלי אתחזק בב"ד וקמ"ל רבותא דמ"מ ביוצא לאחר חתום כשר אלא דסבירא ליה לתוס' כהסמ"ע ואם כן אלו לא אתחזק בב"ד הא יש לו מגו דגייז ואף כי שאומר דלא נפרע נאמן כמ"ש הסמ"ע ועכצ"ל דכבר אתחזק בב"ד ותו לא מצי לגוז אותו וה"ל מגו למפרע ואם כן אף בשליש הדין כן וא"ש דהוי תיובת' דאם נדחוק בסברא בעלמא אין זה מספיק לומר תיובתא אבל לפמ"ש נכון ונר' דברים שס"ל תוס' כסמ"ע וכן מצאתי באס"ז לב"מ בשם מהרמ"כ דאפילו לאחר חיתום שטרות סמוך לחתימת עדים ממש הרי הוא כשר דאי הוי פסק לי' בתר הכי לא הוי מצי לקיים שטרא אלא בלופופי ניירא אחרינא ואיכא למיחש עלה דשטרא דלמא סמפון הוי בי' והתקרע עכ"ל הרי דמצריך כל כך קרוב לשטר עד שאם יחתכו יהא זיופא בקל ניכר ומירתת אבל בלא"ה לא אם כן הדבר במחלוקת:
urim_vetumim_tumim.en: And even on part of it. Sema holds that this rule applies only where the receipt is written in a place from which it cannot be cut away. If it could have been cut off, the creditor is believed to say the debt was not paid because he has a migo that he could simply have cut off the receipt. Shach cites Hagahot Rosh that no migo applies because it is a migo against a chazakah. It is true that Hagahot Rosh says this, but he cites R. Baruch of Regensburg as disagreeing. It appears that Tosafot in Sanhedrin 31b follow Sema. The Gemara challenges the second version, which requires a migo for a third party, from the Mishnah: if there are no witnesses on the receipt and it emerges from the hand of a third party, the third party is believed. Tosafot say one cannot explain that case as one where the document had not yet been established before beit din, because the clause is parallel to the next clause concerning a receipt written after the signatures. Why not establish both clauses before the document was judicially established? The answer is that if the note had not yet been established before beit din, then where the receipt was written on the document itself the creditor would have a migo that he could cut it off. He could then deny payment. Thus the Mishnah's novelty would disappear. We must therefore be speaking after the document was established before beit din, when cutting the receipt would create a retroactive migo and would not help. This strongly indicates that Tosafot accept Sema's migo. I likewise found in Shitah Mekubetzet to Bava Metzia, in the name of Maharam of Rothenburg, that even a receipt written immediately after the witnesses' signatures is valid only if it lies so close to the signatures that cutting it off would make the document visibly suspicious or require attaching another sheet. If it could be removed cleanly, the concern remains that the creditor could cut it away. Thus the matter is genuinely disputed, but Sema has substantial support.

urim_vetumim_urim.he:
ואפי' במקצתו דעת הסמ"ע דצריך להיות השובר נכתב באופן דא"א לחתוך השובר דאם יחתוך יהיה זיופו ניכר אבל בזה אופן דאפשר לחתוך הרי יש לו מגו דחתכו והוא נאמן דאין בשובר ממש והש"ך השיג דהוי מגו במקום חזקה ועיין תומים דבררתי דהוא מחלוקת רבוות' ומידי ספיקא דדינא לא נפקא והממע"ה:
וה"ה אם מצא כתוב וכו' לדעת סמ"ע צ"ל באופן דליכא מגו דאחרי' ראו הפנקס ומצאו בתוכו שתו ל"ל מגו אבל ביש מגו דגונזו נאמן במגו:
urim_vetumim_urim.en:
Even in part. Sema says the receipt must be written in a manner such that cutting it off would visibly reveal forgery. If it could simply be cut away without leaving evidence, the holder has a migo that he could have cut it away and is therefore believed to say the receipt has no force. Shach objects that this is a migo against a presumption. See Tumim. I show that the matter is disputed among major authorities and remains an unresolved monetary doubt. The burden of proof is on the claimant.
“If he found a book, and so on, he said, ‘Go forth from the mouth of his hand, see the peso and find him drunk in him, but he has a faithful grain in his body:

mechaber.he: ראובן נפטר ונמצא בא' משטרותיו מכתב ידו שטר זה פרוע או שנפרע כך וכך עושים כמו שכתוב בשובר:
mechaber.en: If Reuven died and his own handwriting is found on one of his documents stating, 'This document is paid,' or, 'Such-and-such amount was paid,' the notation is treated as a receipt.

baer_hetev.he: ונמצא. בע"ש כתב דאיירי דנמצא מונח כתב בתוך השטר וכתוב עליו כן ע"ש ואין טעם נכון לדבריו אלא דקמ"ל המחבר דאף שנכתב השובר במקום שיכול לחתכו עושין כמו שכתוב בשובר כיון שהן יתומים וטוענין שמא ואין טענינן בזה עבורם משא"כ כשהוא חי וטוען ברי כמש"ל עכ"ל הסמ"ע: אבל הש"ך כתב דל"נ פירושו אלא דהמחבר מיירי כפשוטו דאע"פ שכתב לעיל דשובר בגופו של שטר כשר כתבו עוד כאן להורות דאף גבי יורשים הדין כן דה"א דוקא כשהמלוה חי השטר פסול אבל ביורשיו לא דהא בכמה דוכתי יורשים עדיפי ממלו' עצמו קמ"ל וכת' עוד דהב"ח פי' דמיירי שהוא כת"י ממש ולדיוקא אצטריך דאע"ג דאם היה המלו' חי הוה קרעינן לי' אפי' הוא כת"י אחר מ"מ הכא ליכא חזקה דלא מרע כו' ולא נהירא דכיון שנכתב שובר על גוף השטר אף ע"פ שהוא כת"י אחר קרעינן ליה מכח חזקה דלא היה מרע לשטרי' עכ"ל (וכן השיג הט"ז על הב"ח וכתב דדבריו תמוהים דכל שנתקלקל השטר באיז' אופן שיהי' הוה השטר פרוע ע"ש):
baer_hetev.en: And it was found. The Ir Shushan writes that this refers to a separate writing found lying within the promissory note stating this. See there. There is no sound reason for his explanation. Rather, the Mechaber teaches that even if the receipt was written in a place from which it could be cut off, we act in accordance with the receipt, since the holders are heirs who plead only a doubtful claim, and we do not advance a contrary claim for them in this matter, unlike where the lender himself is alive and makes a definite claim, as stated above. Thus writes the Sema. The Shach, however, writes that this explanation does not appear correct. Rather, the Mechaber means the ruling literally. Although he already wrote above that a receipt written on the body of the promissory note is valid, he repeats it here to teach that the same law applies to heirs. One might have thought that only when the lender is alive is the note invalid, but not in the hands of his heirs, since in several areas heirs are in a stronger position than the lender himself. Therefore the Mechaber teaches otherwise. The Shach further writes that the Bach explains this as referring specifically to the lender's own handwriting, and that the wording is needed for an inference: although if the lender were alive we would tear up the note even if the receipt were in another person's handwriting, here there is no presumption that a person would not impair his own document. This is unpersuasive, for once a receipt is written on the body of the promissory note, even if it is in another handwriting, we tear it up based on the presumption that the lender would not have impaired his own note. The Taz likewise objects to the Bach and writes that his words are difficult, because whenever the note has been impaired in any manner, the debt is treated as paid. See there.

beer_hagolah.he: ז) בתשובות הרא"ש כלל ס"ח סי' ס"ה והביאו הטור

beur_hagra.he:
ראובן. כנ"ל בסעי' הקודם ועש"ך:
(ליקוט) ראובן כו'. וקמ"ל דלא טענינן ליתמי. ט"ז וש"ך (ע"כ):
beur_hagra.en:
Reuven. As stated in the preceding seif. See the Shach.
(Supplement) Reuven. It teaches that we do not advance this claim on behalf of the orphans. Taz and Shach. (End of supplement.)

meirat_einayim.he: ראובן נפטר ונמצא כו' עמ"ש לפני זה פירושו ובע"ש כתב דאיירי דנמצא מונח כתב בתוך השטר חוב וכתב עליו כן ע"ש ואין טעם נכון לדבריו וגם לדברי המחבר נראה כמו שכתבתי:
meirat_einayim.en: Noah died and was found to be a pharaoh before this means that, according to the letter, he wrote, “There is no reason for him, and that the author also seems like I wrote:

netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.he: ונמצא. בכאן אפילו להסמ"ע לעיל ס"ק נ"ט כשר השובר כיון שהוא מת ולהש"ך אפילו חי ונקט יורשים לרבותא דלפעמים יורשים עדיפא ודין זה הוא אפילו בכת"י אחר. ש"ך:
netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.en: and found. In here, even to the above paragraph, the psalmist, who is dead and who has even lived and taken heirs, including sometimes heirs to the Fa and this sentence is even in another tier. “Third:

siftei_kohen.he: ראובן נפטר כו' עושים כמו שכתוב בשובר. כתב העיר שושן דמיירי דנמצא מונח כתב בתוך השטר דאל"כ היינו מ"ש בסעיף הקודם ולא נהירא דעיקר חסר מן הספר ועוד דא"כ מנ"ל להמחבר זה הא בתשובת הרא"ש מיירי להדיא שכתוב בגוף השטר ועוד דסתמא אמרי' בש"ס ספ"ק דמציע' וכן לעיל סעיף י"ח סמפון היוצא מתחת ידי מלוה כשר ולא מפליגינן בין נמצא מונח בתוך השטר או לא ועוד דא"כ מאי פריך בש"ס התם מכל הנך משניות ה"ל לשנויי דמיירי שנמצא מונח תוך השטר אלא ודאי אין חילוק ולעולם אמרינן דלמא המלוה היה צריך גוף השטר לשום ענין והכין השובר ליתנו לו כשיפרע. והסמ"ע פי' דמיירי אף שהשובר כתוב למטה במקום שהיה יכול לחתכו וקמ"ל דאף שהמלוה היה גובה בו אין טוענים בזה נגד היתומים ואין דבריו נכונים ובפרט לפי מ"ש בסמוך ס"ק ע"א דגם המלוה לא היה גובה בו והב"ח פי' דמיירי שהוא כתב ידו ממש ולדיוקא אצטריך דאם הוא אינו כתב ידו אין עושין כמ"ש בשובר אלא יהא מונח עד שיבוא אליהו דאע"ג דאם היה המלוה חי היה קרעינן ליה אפי' הוא כתב יד אחר מ"מ הכא ליכא חזקה דלא מרע אינש לשטריה כיון דספק הוא אם נכתב שובר זה בחייו או לא עכ"ד וגם זה אינו נכון כלל גם דינו לא נהירא דכיון שנכתב שובר על גוף השטר אע"פ שהוא כ"י אחר קרעינן ליה מכת חזקה דאי איתא דלא נפרע לא היה מרע לשטריה וכן משמע ברמב"ם ס"פ י"ו מה' מלוה ע"ש בדין ט' ובדין י' ודוק. אלא נראה דהמחבר מיירי כפשוטו ואע"פ שכתב בסעיף הקודם דשובר בגופו של שטר כשר הביא בכאן ל' תשובת הרא"ש להורות דאף גבי יורשים הדין כן דהא בכמה דוכתי יורשים עדיפים ממלוה עצמו וגם לעיל ס"ק ס"ב אמרי' דמלוה אינו גובה ויורשיו גובים א"כ ה"א דוקא כשהמלוה חי השטר פסול אבל ביורשיו לא דדלמא אי הוה אבוהון קיים הוה מברר דכשלא כדין או בטעות או לרשימה בעלמא נכתב וכה"ג קמ"ל:
siftei_kohen.en: Reuven died, etc. We follow what is written in the receipt. Ir Shushan’s claim that the writing must have been found physically inserted within the document is unsupported and would omit the essential fact from the text. The Rosh’s responsum expressly concerns a receipt written on the document itself, and the Gemara makes no distinction between one placed inside the document and one found elsewhere. The Sema’s explanation that the novelty concerns a receipt written where it could have been cut away is also incorrect, especially because even the living creditor could not collect in that case. The Bach’s limitation to the creditor’s own handwriting is likewise unsound. A receipt written on the body of the document invalidates it even in another hand, because one does not ordinarily impair his own document unless payment occurred. The Mechaber cites the Rosh here to teach that the same applies to heirs. One might otherwise have argued that heirs are sometimes in a stronger position and could claim that their father would have explained that the receipt was written mistakenly, unlawfully, or merely as a notation. The ruling rejects that argument.

urim_vetumim_urim.he: עושי' כמ"ש בשובר כתב הסמ"ע דקמ"ל בזה אף שכבר כתבו בסעי' הקודם משום דבמלוה חי בעינן באופן דלית ליה מגו אבל ביורשים אף דהיה להם מגו דגנזו הכתב מכל מקום עושים כמו שכתוב והש"ך כ' דקמ"ל דה"א יורשי' עדיף כחם ממלוה גופי' אולי כיון דמלוה יכול להשביע ללוה שפרע וה"א דאף ליורשי' נטעון כמו שהיה אפשר למלוה לטעון ויצטרך הלוה לישבע קמ"ל דאפילו שבועה א"צ ויעשה כמ"ש בשובר:
urim_vetumim_urim.en: We act. As written in the receipt. Sema writes that this is repeated even though it was already stated in the preceding seif because where the lender is alive the law may depend on a circumstance in which he lacks a migo, whereas with heirs, even if they would have had a migo to conceal the writing, we nevertheless act according to what the receipt says. Shach writes that the novelty is that one might have thought the heirs have greater strength than the lender himself. Perhaps because the lender could have required the borrower to swear that he paid, we would make the same claim for his heirs and require the borrower to swear. The law therefore teaches that even an oath is unnecessary and we act according to the receipt.

mechaber.he: מי שמת ונמצא באחד משטרותיו מכתב ידו שטר זה חציו לפלוני אין לאותו פלו' חלק בו:
mechaber.en: Those who die and are in one of his regimes a letter of his hand that has not been divided into the bottom of the balloon have no part in it:

baer_hetev.he: חלק. ול"ד לשטר שנכתב עליו פרעון דהתם מגרע השטר בכתיב' זו ואמרינן דלא הי' כותב כך אם אינו אמת וע"ל סימן פ"א סי"ז וי"ח. סמ"ע:
baer_hetev.en: Part. And he said, “He who has been written against him is not true and is not a sign of Hashem.” A:

beer_hagolah.he: ח) שם ושם מטעם דאפילו אמר כן בפני עדים ולא אמר אתם עדים היה יכול לומר שלא להשביע את עצמי עשיתי
beer_hagolah.en: There and there, for Dach, he said yes to witnesses, and you could not say that I did not satisfy myself

beur_hagra.he: מי. סנה' כ"ט ב' וע"ל סי' פ"א:
beur_hagra.en: Who. Sana as “T. B” and C.P

meirat_einayim.he: אין לאותו פלוני חלק בו. דלא עדיף האי כתב מאלו אמר כן בפני עדים ולא אמר אתם עדי דאמרי' שלא להשביעו כ"כ וע"ל הי' פ"א מ"ש עוד מזה ול"ד לשטר שנכתב עליו פרעון דהתם מגרע השטר בכתיבה זו דכשיוצא השטר בב"ד לגבות בו רואין עליו פרעון הלכך אמרינן דלא היה כותב אותו אם אינו אמת ע"ש:
meirat_einayim.en: That person has no share in it. This writing is no stronger than if the decedent had said the same thing before witnesses without saying, "You are my witnesses," in which case we say that he spoke merely so as not to appear wealthy. See also siman 81 for what I wrote further on this. This is unlike a debt instrument upon which a payment notation is written. There, the writing detracts from the force of the document itself, because when the document is produced in beit din for collection, the payment notation is visible on it. Therefore we say that the creditor would not have written it unless it were true. See there.

netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.he: חלק. ול"ד לכתוב עליו פרעה דהתם מגרע גרע השטר בכתיבה זו אמרי' דלא הי' כותב אם אינו אמת:
netivot_hamishpat_hidushim.en: Blank. This is unlike writing upon the document that it was paid. There, the very act of writing weakens the note, and we say he would not have written it unless true.

siftei_kohen.he: אין לאותו פלו' כו'. ע"ל סי' פ"א סעיף י"ז וי"ח מ"ש בזה:
siftei_kohen.en: That particular person has no, etc. See above, siman 81, seifim 17 and 18, and what I wrote there on this matter.

mechaber.he: האומר שטר בין שטרותי פרוע ואיני יודע איזהו כל שטרותיו פרועים נמצא לאחד שם שנים הגדול פרוע ולא הקטן (נ"י סוף ב"ב): הגה אבל אם נמצא שובר בבית לוה על הקטן ודאי הקטן פרוע ולא הגדול (נ"י) וכן אם לא אמר א' פרוע אלא אומר שטר אחד מחול לך הקטן מחול ולא הגדול (מה"ר דוד כהן בית כ' סי' ו'):
mechaber.en: It is said that a bill between my wild notes and I don't know which of his wild notes is one of the great, wild, and not the little ones (Genesis at the end of the B): The pronunciation, but if you're in the house of Loa for the small, wild little, and not the great (N.A.) and if you don't say a single note to you from the small dance, and not the great (from David Cohen House)

baer_hetev.he:
יודע. לאו דוקא שאומר בפי' איני יודע אלא כל שלא בירר לבניו איזהו הדין כן כ"כ הנ"י: ש"ך:
מחול. פי' הסמ"ע הטעם דמחיל' ה"ל כמתנה והזוכ' הוא בא להוציא ועליו להביא ראי' וכתב הש"ך דכ"ז כשידוע בבירור או הלו' מודה שמחלו לו בחנם אבל באומר סתם מחול לך והלוה טוען ברי שהיה מחוייב למחול לו דמי לפרעון והגדול מחול והרב קיצר בדבר עכ"ל:
baer_hetev.en:
Knows. This does not specifically mean that he explicitly says, 'I do not know.' Rather, whenever the father did not identify for his sons which debt was paid, the same law applies. So writes the Nimukei Yosef. Shach.
Forgiven. The Sema explains that forgiveness is like a gift, and the beneficiary seeks to extract property, so the burden of proof is upon him. The Shach writes that this applies only where it is clearly known, or the borrower admits, that the lender forgave the debt gratuitously. But if the lender merely said, 'It is forgiven to you,' and the borrower makes a definite claim that the lender was obligated to forgive it, it is treated like repayment, and the larger debt is deemed forgiven. Rama stated the matter briefly.

beur_hagra.en:
But if. It is not known, but it is known, and it is not for years, but if it is. This is the same as one
(Likkut) And likewise. Here we do not say that the holder of the document has the inferior position, as we do regarding a sale in the Gemara there.
Proof for this position is that waiver and emancipation share one rule, as Tosafot write in the first chapter of Sanhedrin and Sefer HaTerumot in gate 51. See there. The Tosefta in Bava Batra likewise teaches that one who says, Let Tavi my slave be made free, and one who says, Give, are governed differently from a promissory note, as explained above.
(Likkut) And likewise if. As stated in the Tosefta at the end of Bava Batra regarding emancipation, and the same applies to waiver, since emancipation is a form of waiver, as stated in the first chapter of Kiddushin. The Shach objects that with a receipt the language is construed in favor of the holder, as stated in siman 42, seif 8, and even regarding waiver, as stated in siman 43, seifim 25 and 27. This is not correct. Certainly the written language of a receipt is construed in favor of its holder, as stated there, 171b, where it was written without qualification, applying whenever the stated condition occurs. But when a person's right rests upon his oral statement, the language is construed narrowly, as stated in siman 71, seif 21. This ruling supports the Rif's decision there. See there. (End of supplement.)

Rather, he says, "One document is forgiven to you," etc. Forgiveness is legally comparable to a gift. The person seeking to benefit from it is the one who seeks to remove property from the giver's possession, and therefore the burden of proof is upon him.

He knows. Meaning, even if he did not expressly say so, but simply failed to clarify for his heirs which debt was involved, the law is the same. Shach.
Waived. Waiver is like a gift, and the one claiming the waiver seeks to extract from the original presumption, so the burden of proof is upon him. Sema. This applies specifically where it is known that the lender waived the debt gratuitously. But if the borrower asserts with certainty that the lender was obligated to waive it, the case resembles repayment, and the larger amount is treated as waived. Shach.

pitchei_teshuva.en:
The smaller amount is waived. In the glosses of Rabbi Akiva Eiger to Shulchan Aruch it is written: This applies because the uncertainty concerns how much was waived. If the amount waived is known, but there is a legal doubt whether the waiver is effective, then at first glance the obligor should be exempt because of the doubt. However, from Beit Shmuel, siman 66, seif katan 9, it appears that he does not agree. In my humble opinion, this requires study. See Nimukei Yosef, first chapter of Bava Batra, concerning one who established a right to place beams, where it appears that even if the doubt concerns the waiver itself, namely whether a waiver occurred, and the issue is a legal doubt, the party in possession prevails. Likewise, Shulchan Aruch Even HaEzer, siman 106, rules that even where the woman is healthy, in an unresolved Talmudic question whether she waived her kesubah, the heirs prevail. The Rif there, however, actually holds that because of doubt she does not lose her kesubah. End of quote.

siftei_kohen.he:
ואיני יודע כו'. לאו דוקא אומר בפירוש איני יודע אלא כל שלא בירר לבניו איזהו הדין כן כ"כ הנמוק"י:
כל שטרותיו כו' ואין חילוק בדינים אלו בין שהמלוה חי או שמת אח"כ אלא דאם הוא חי וטוען אח"כ עיינתי ונזכרתי שזה פרוע והאחרים אינם פרועים חוזר וגובה בהן כדלעיל סי' נ"ט וע"ש:
אבל אם נמצא שובר כו'. הקטן פרוע ולא הגדול וה"ה השטרות שעל הלווים האחרים אינן פרועים דאמרינן אותו שטר שיש ביד לוה זה שובר עליו הי' פרוע ולא האחרים וכן הוא בנמוק"י להדיא ומביאו ב"י:
אלא אומר שטר אחד מחול לך כו'. כ"כ מהרדיך שמדמה זה למכר דלקמן ס"ס רי"ח ומביאו ב"י ולפע"ד לא דמי דהתם המוכר מוחזק בשדהו אבל הכא המקבל מוחזק במעות ודמי לפרוע ומה"ט אמרינן לעיל סי' מ"ב סעיף ח' דאף בשובר אמרי' דיד בעל השובר על העליונה אף נגד שטר אע"פ שכתוב בשובר לשון מחילה וכדאיתא בס' מ"ג סעיף כ"ה וסעיף כ"ו ע"ש וצל"ע: ומ"מ נראה דאף מהרד"ך לא קאמר אלא כשידוע בבירור או שהלוה מודה שמחל לו בחנם ומטעם שכתב שם שהקונה או המקבל מתנה על ידו התחתונ' והיינו דכתב מהרד"ך שם באומר שטר לך בידי מחול שמחלתיו לך כו' אבל באומר סתם מחול לך והלוה טוען ברי ואומר שמחל לו מחמת שהיה מחויב למחול לו דמי לפרעון והגדול מחול והר"ב קיצר בדבר ודוק:
שטר אחד מחול לך כו'. ע"ל סי' רמ"א סעיף ב' בהג"ה ומ"ש שם:
siftei_kohen.en:
And I do not know, etc. This does not mean that he must expressly say, “I do not know.” Rather, whenever he failed to clarify to his heirs which particular document was paid, the same law applies. So writes Nimukei Yosef.
All of his documents, etc. There is no distinction in these laws between a creditor who is still alive and one who later died. If he is alive and afterward says, “I reviewed the matter and remembered that this particular document was paid and the others were not,” he may again collect with the others, as above, siman 59; see there.
But if a receipt is found, etc. The smaller debt is deemed paid, not the larger one. The same applies to documents against other borrowers: they are not deemed paid. We say that the receipt found in this borrower’s possession related to one document against this borrower, and not to the others. This is explicit in Nimukei Yosef, cited by Beit Yosef.
Rather, he says: One document is forgiven to you, etc. Maharik writes this, comparing it to the law of a sale below, at the end of siman 218, and Beit Yosef cites him. In my humble opinion, the comparison is not exact. There, the seller is in possession of his land, whereas here the recipient is in possession of the money. It is more comparable to payment. For this reason we say above, siman 42, seif 8, that even regarding a receipt the hand of the receipt holder is on the upper side against the document, even though the receipt uses language of waiver, as in siman 43, seifim 25 and 26. This requires further study. Nevertheless, it appears that even Maharik says this only where it is clearly known, or the borrower admits, that the creditor gratuitously forgave the document, for the reason he gives there that the purchaser or recipient of a gift has the lower hand. This is why Maharik there speaks of one who says, “A document that I hold against you is forgiven, for I forgave it to you.” But where he merely says, “It is forgiven to you,” and the borrower makes a definite claim that the creditor forgave it because he was obligated to do so, it resembles payment, and the larger debt is deemed forgiven. The Rama abbreviated the matter. Examine carefully.
One document is forgiven to you, etc. See below, siman 241, seif 2, in the gloss, and what I write there.

The smaller amount is waived. The debtor admits he never actually paid or received an express waiver. He relies only on ambiguous wording and claims that by its language the smaller amount was waived. Since the language itself is doubtful, this is like saying, “I do not know whether I paid you,” and he remains liable. See my Kuntres HaTefisot and siman 75 concerning whether one who says, “I do not know whether I paid,” is liable even where he had no reason to know. This case proves that liability remains.
